title: Assay SDK: integration cheat sheet & debug notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note is a compact, practical reference for engineers integrating a new model into the Assay eval harness. Goal: give the minimum scaffolding that gets a model from `local-run -> CI smoke -> gated regression` with sensible defaults, plus troubleshooting heuristics. Use this as a quick-start and living checklist rather than a finished spec.

High-level flow (one-liner):
1) add prompt set + canonical metadata -> 2) implement dataset loader -> 3) add scoring functions + baseline cases -> 4) local runner smoke -> 5) CI job + gating thresholds -> 6) post-merge nightly regression.

Quick checklist (copy to PR template):
- [ ] Add promptset file under `assays/prompt-sets/<family>/<model-version>-v1.jsonl` with canonical IDs
- [ ] Implement dataset loader in `assays/loaders/<family>_loader.py` registering with AssayLoaderRegistry
- [ ] Add unit tests for loader: size, example shape, tokenization sanity
- [ ] Add scoring adapters in `assays/scorers/` (exact, fuzzy, embedding-sim)
- [ ] Provide baseline outputs (gold/expected) for 50 canonical prompts (small sample) in `assays/benchmarks/`
- [ ] Add CI smoke in `.github/workflows/evals-<model>.yml` referencing test dataset (use small fixtures)
- [ ] Define gating rules in `assays/gates/<model>.yaml` (metric + delta relative to baseline)

Practical tips for prompt sets:
- Use a small, curated canonical set for CI (30–100 prompts). Keep the full prompt bank (>1k) in a separate file for nightly/regression runs.
- Each prompt entry schema: id, intent_tags (list), ctx (optional), template, expected_audit_flag (opt). Example: 
  {
    "id": "summ-001",
    "intent_tags": ["summarization", "finance"],
    "template": "Summarize the following earnings note: {{ doc }}"
  }
- Prefer explicit seeds or deterministic sampler for any stochastic prompt variants so CI runs are reproducible.
- Add negative controls and adversarial perturbations as a small companion file `*_neg.jsonl` to catch hallucination/regression.

Loader design patterns (common mistakes to avoid):
- Keep loader pure: it should map on-disk artifact -> canonical example tuple (prompt_id, prompt_text, metadata). Avoid network calls/credentials during loading.
- Implement `prefetch(n)` and `sample(seed, n)` hooks used by the local runner to create deterministic splits.
- Tokenization sanity: return both `raw_text` and `token_ids` from the loader where feasible; ensures scoring functions that depend on length don't re-tokenize with divergent tokenizers.
- Support `metadata.tags` for filtering (e.g., smoke_only).

Scoring functions (recommendations):
- Keep scorers orthogonal and small; compose higher-level metrics in the report generator.
- Minimal set for text tasks: exact_match, normalized_levenshtein, tokenized_f1 (wordpieces), embedding_cosine (sentence-transformer).
- For generation diversity tasks: self-BLEU, distinct-n (n=2,3) and length-distribution-kde.
- For closed-answer tasks: answer-extraction + normalized numeric compare (float tolerance param).
- Example pseudocode for embedding-based scorer: 
  def embedding_cosine_score(gold, pred):
      e_gold = embed(gold)
      e_pred = embed(pred)
      return cosine(e_gold, e_pred)
  Notes: cache embeddings for gold; use the same embedding model across baseline and candidate runs.

Baseline and regression rules:
- Baseline profiles live in `assays/baselines/<model-family>/<baseline-name>.json` and include metric medians and 90th-percentile latency.
- Gate config example: 
  - metric: exact_match
    mode: absolute
    threshold: 0.85
    allow_regress_pct: 0.01  # allow small flakiness
  - metric: embedding_cosine
    mode: relative
    delta_pct: -3  # model under test must not drop >3% from baseline median
- CI gating policy: fail only on absolute failures (safety/integrity). For quality metrics, prefer warning in PR and fail only if delta > 5% or if p-value < 0.01 after bootstrapping.

CI wiring (github actions snippets and practical setup):
- Job names: `evals-smoke`, `evals-gate`, `evals-nightly` (nightly runs scheduled in a separate workflow with larger resources).
- Minimal GH Action job: 
  name: Eval smoke
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    - name: Setup python
      uses: actions/setup-python@v4
      with: python-version: 3.10
    - name: Install deps
      run: pip install -r assays/requirements.txt
    - name: Run small evals
      run: assays/run_eval --loader assays/loaders/<family>_loader:Smoke --promptset assays/prompt-sets/<family>/ci-sample.jsonl --scorers exact_match,embedding_cosine --out results/smoke.json
    - name: Compare to baseline
      run: assays/compare results/smoke.json assays/baselines/<family>/ci-baseline.json --gates assays/gates/<model>.yaml
- Use job matrix for families or quantization variants but avoid exploding matrix size in PRs. For heavy models, CI should call a hosted inference stub (see stubs section).

Hosted inference stubs and offline mode:
- For gated PRs avoid using real heavy GPUs. Provide a light stub that mimics API surface and deterministic responses for smoke prompts. Place in `assays/stubs/` and reference it in CI.
- Stubs should also include latency floor simulations to catch perf regressions in latency-aware gates.

Flakiness and stability heuristics:
- Track test-level variance over time (rolling 30-day stdev) and mark examples as `flaky` if stdev > threshold. Exclude flaky examples from gate calculations or use them only in informational reports.
- Implement bootstrap-based p-values for metric deltas when sample size < 200. Add `--bootstrap 1000` in compare tool for small samples.

Reporting and triage notes after a failed gate:
- Auto-generate a condensed HTML report: top 10 regressions by absolute delta, counterexamples, and a diff view (gold vs pred).
- Include a quick reproduction command in the report pointing to a git commit, prompt id, and a single-run script.
- Suggested triage steps: rerun with `--seed` to confirm, run against baseline model to check baseline shift, check tokenization and locale settings.

Common pitfalls and gotchas (war stories):
- Tokenizer mismatch: one of the more frequent causes of small deltas. Always freeze tokenizer version in model metadata and loader.
- Hidden randomness in post-processing (e.g., trimming punctuation) can cause flaky exact match failures. Add a canonical normalizer util and use it everywhere.
- Latency/regression noise from infra: isolate perf gates to nightly/longer windows rather than PR smoke.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we adopt a single canonical embedding model for all embedding-based scorers or allow per-family overrides? (short term: canonical for baseline comparability)
- Policy for retiring promptset examples when they are marked flaky by >3 independent model runs.
- Better tooling for interactive counterexample inspection inside PRs (embedding nearest neighbor viewer).

References and quick links:
- Local runner: `assays/run_eval --help`
- Loader contract: see `assays/loaders/README.md` (defines tuple shape and registration)
- Baseline format: `assays/baselines/README.md`

Contact for help: Maya (owner), Diego (loader patterns), Priya (CI and gating), Jonah (reporting).

Appendix: small loader skeleton (python):
  class ExampleLoader(BaseAssayLoader):
      """Return iterator over canonical examples: dicts with keys id, prompt, gold, metadata"""
      def __init__(self, path):
          self.path = path
      def __iter__(self):
          with open(self.path) as f:
              for line in f:
                  row = json.loads(line)
                  yield {
                      'id': row['id'],
                      'prompt': row['template'].format(**row.get('ctx', {})),
                      'gold': row.get('gold', None),
                      'metadata': row.get('meta', {})
                  }

Keep this doc as the quick pragmatic cheat-sheet; feed back improvements into the canonical confluence page when patterns stabilize.
